value.title: Cross-model review — rs-boot-announce (135), phase 1, round 1 (post-merge)
value.note: VERDICT: material findings — 2 MAJOR, 3 MINOR, 2 NIT. Plan 135 is ALREADY MERGED (main 4b000ffb, no-ff merge of fef83b97; reviewed at main tip 5b40ed76, diffed against merge parent 59748c17). Both MAJOR findings are real and one of them means MAIN IS RED. f1: the golden fixture was relocated to crates/testkit/fixtures/ and the Rust half of AC4's shared-fixture citation was never updated, so three pij-daemon tests panic with NotFound on the merged tree — AC4 is false as stated and AC6's `cargo test --workspace green` is false on main. Reported early; the PM reproduced it, found the root cause (a `git add` whose file list named the already-moved path, aborting the whole add, with stderr sent to /dev/null — the composed `cargo test --workspace` then went green against a WORKING tree that differed from the COMMITTED one), and fixed it on the branch at 99269b90 by resolving the fixture through `pij_testkit::fixtures::read` so a future move is a compile error rather than a runtime NotFound. That fix was NOT on main when this record was written. f2 is a composition-seam defect that survives the merge: the register handler now overwrites a caller-asserted process identity with a pane-derived one, and when the harness-child walk fails it silently substitutes the PANE SHELL, which for a stable pane yields `binding: same` for a genuinely new harness process — the exact announce-suppression bug this plan exists to remove — while `proc_source`, the field that would expose it, has ZERO consumers anywhere. WHAT I DID NOT TAKE ON TRUST: I re-derived AC5's RED independently by extracting the merge parent with `git archive` into /tmp/pij-base-135, copying only the NEW test files and the fixture onto it, and running them — 12 of the new witnesses fail there, including both announce-count assertions and the u3 same-pane guard. I re-ran the daemon, store and extension suites myself. I probed the frame grammar empirically rather than by reading the regex. And I am my own live witness for AC1 and AC8: this reviewer seat is a `pij-rs spawn --harness omp` seat whose FIRST injected turn was announceText, and whose inbound peer messages arrived as `[pij-rs from pij-verbal-silverfish]` … `[/pij]`. Seven KNOWN-OPEN items from the dispatch packet consumed zero findings. READ-ONLY on code throughout; the only file written is this record. ADDENDUM (written after main advanced under this review): f1 is CLOSED on main at c46e2495 — aa697235 merged the testkit-helper fix, and I re-derived the green myself (4/4 daemon binding tests) rather than accepting it. AC4 and AC6 were correctly downgraded to unchecked by the PM and re-earned from `git show HEAD` on the merge target rather than from disk, which is the exact discipline whose absence caused the defect. Six items remain open — f2 (MAJOR), f3, f4, f5 (MINOR), n1 and n2 (NIT); none of them was introduced or affected by the fix. ROUND-1 POSTSCRIPT: my own remedy (a) for f2 was WITHDRAWN and replaced before any fix was built — see f2's correction. It would have re-admitted a wire-asserted pid at the exact moment daemon-derived evidence failed, re-opening one branch over the anti-impersonation control that identity.rs:436-450 had already carved out. The replacement demotes the claim from EVIDENCE to a SELECTOR among processes the daemon observed for itself (a live descendant of the pane root), which is the distinction the doctrine actually turns on. Recorded because a reviewer's proposed fix deserves the same scepticism as an author's, and mine did not survive it.

value.finding: MAIN IS RED, and the failure is in the very seam AC4 exists to protect. Commit c5069fe0 moved the golden fixture from docs/plans/135-rs-boot-announce/assets/contracts/register-response.json to crates/testkit/fixtures/register-response.json (a good move — the builder flow archives plan folders at post-flight and two live suites read this file at test time). Its commit message asserts "AC4's property is preserved exactly: one file, both suites citing the same path." That assertion is false. The TypeScript half was updated (adapters/rust-runtime.test.ts:32 → `new URL("../../../../crates/testkit/fixtures/register-response.json", import.meta.url)`); the Rust half was not (crates/daemon/src/http/tests.rs:445 still joins CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR with `../../docs/plans/135-rs-boot-announce/assets/contracts/register-response.json`). That directory now contains only README.md, so `std::fs::read_to_string(...).expect("read shared register response fixture")` panics. THREE consequences, all against the plan's own promises: (1) AC4 is FALSE as stated — the two suites do not cite the same path, and the Rust one cites a path with no file behind it; (2) AC6's `cargo test --workspace green on the composed branch` is FALSE on the merged tree, and this is not a timing artifact — it is a deterministic ENOENT; (3) the same aborted stage left docs/plans/135-rs-boot-announce/assets/contracts/README.md still declaring "Path both sides cite: docs/plans/135-rs-boot-announce/assets/contracts/register-response.json", so the contract document points at nothing. The one piece of good news is the shape of the failure: `.expect()` makes it a hard panic, so it can never pass silently. PM root cause, supplied on refutation and worth recording because it generalises: the commit's `git add` file list named the OLD path, which no longer existed, so the ENTIRE add aborted — and `2>/dev/null` swallowed the error. tests.rs and the README were never staged. The composed `cargo test --workspace` then ran green against a working tree that was not the committed tree. FIXED on branch 135-rs-boot-announce at 99269b90, taking the structural option rather than the one-token one: the daemon test now resolves the fixture through `pij_testkit::fixtures::read("register-response.json")`, so a future relocation is a COMPILE error. Not yet on main at the time of this record. ADDENDUM, re-derived by me on main after the fix landed rather than accepted from the PM's report: main is now c46e2495, carrying aa697235 (merge of 99269b90). crates/daemon/src/http/tests.rs:450 now reads `serde_json::from_str(&pij_testkit::fixtures::read("register-response.json"))` — no relative path string survives — and `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 cargo test -p pij-daemon --lib registration_binding` run by me on that tree returns `test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed`. The contract README now reads "Path both sides cite: crates/testkit/fixtures/register-response.json". Both halves of this finding are closed on main. Worth recording that the helper is strictly stronger than a corrected path: `pij_testkit::fixtures::read` resolves through the MANIFEST corpus, which re-hashes entries, so a future relocation is a compile error and a future edit-in-place is a hash failure — the path-string form had already failed once in exactly the silent way.
value.receipt: Run by me at main 5b40ed76: `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 cargo test -p pij-daemon --lib registration_binding` → `test result: FAILED. 1 passed; 3 failed; 0 ignored; 171 filtered out`, each failure `panicked at crates/daemon/src/http/tests.rs:447:48: read shared register response fixture: Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound, message: "No such file or directory" }` for registration_binding_{created,rebound,same}_matches_shared_fixture. `ls docs/plans/135-rs-boot-announce/assets/contracts/` → README.md only. `git log --diff-filter=A -- crates/testkit/fixtures/register-response.json` → c5069fe0. AFTER FIX, run by me at c46e2495: `cargo test -p pij-daemon --lib registration_binding` → 4 passed, 0 failed; `grep -rn register-response.json crates/ --include=*.rs` → only tests.rs:450 via the testkit helper.

value.finding: COMPOSITION SEAM u3→u1: a silent pane-shell fallback can re-create the exact bug this plan exists to remove, and the field that would expose it is read by nobody. Three facts compose into one defect. (1) `register` now OVERWRITES the caller's asserted identity: whenever `claim.pane` is present and `claim.harness` parses, it sets `request.claim.pid` and `request.claim.proc_start` from `pane_harness_identity(...)`, discarding what the caller asserted. For an adopt that is exactly right — pane evidence must beat an assertion, that is AC7. For a SELF-REGISTERING harness (omp/pi, whose extension knows its own pid exactly, and sends it) it is a strict downgrade of evidence quality. (2) When the descendant walk finds no harness child, `harness_process_from_snapshot` returns `Some(root)` — the PANE PROCESS — and `pane_harness_identity` labels it `ProcSource::Pane`. (3) `proc_source` has ZERO consumers: it appears only in crates/daemon/src/http/{mod.rs,identity.rs} and their tests. It is not in the TypeScript `RustSeatDescriptor`, not in `pij-rs state`, not in `pij list`. So a seat bound to a pane shell is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a correctly bound one at every operator surface. Compose them: for a pane whose root process is stable (an ordinary login shell) and whose harness child is not recognised, every registration writes the SAME shell identity, so `previous_proc == descriptor.proc`, so `binding: same`, so `fresh = false`, so NO ANNOUNCE for a genuinely new harness process. That is plan 135's own defect, reintroduced through the u3 seam and invisible while it happens. REACHABILITY, which is the part I chased rather than asserted: `harness_command` accepts an interpreter only when the executable basename is exactly `node` or `bun`. On THIS machine the real basename executing the omp package is `bun.exe` — eight live processes of the form `/Users/jordanknight/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/bun/bin/bun.exe /Users/jordanknight/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent/dist/cli.js …`. So the `script.contains(package) && name in {cli,index}` branch CANNOT fire against the launcher this machine actually uses; recognition survives today only by the other branch, because the npm shim `~/.npm-global/bin/omp` gives `file_stem == "omp"`. The package-path branch is exercised only by synthetic strings in the unit test (`node /opt/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/cli.js`) — a fixture authored by its own consumer, which is precisely the trap crates/testkit/fixtures/uds/README.md warns about in this repo's own words. SMALLEST FIX, in the order I would take them: (a) when `pane_harness_identity` returns `ProcSource::Pane` AND the caller asserted its own pid/proc_start, KEEP THE CLAIM rather than overwriting it with the pane shell — adopt carries no claim, so AC7 is untouched, and a self-registering harness stops being demoted to its shell; (b) give `proc_source` a consumer — surface it in `pij-rs state`/`pij list` so a pane-bound seat is visible instead of silent; (c) widen the interpreter allowlist beyond exact `node`/`bun`, or match the package path without requiring a recognised interpreter at all. CORRECTION TO MY OWN REMEDY (a), written after the PM asked whether the fix could introduce a new way to bind wrong — it could, and the hazard is in my wording, so I am withdrawing it. Remedy (a) as first stated ('keep the caller's claim when the source is Pane') would re-admit a WIRE-ASSERTED process identity exactly when the daemon's own evidence failed. `register` accepts an asserted pair from the wire (crates/cli/src/main.rs:109-114 exposes `--pid` and `--proc-start`), and today the unconditional pane override is what neutralises it for paned registrations. The only surviving check is registration.rs:67-87, which proves the claimed process is ALIVE and nothing more — there is no test that it relates to the pane, so a live-but-unrelated process could claim a paned seat whenever the harness walk misses. The repo already argued this against me at identity.rs:436-450: 'Bind evidence is the ANTI-IMPERSONATION control, and a control whose input the SUBJECT SUPPLIES is not a control … Accepting a claim meanwhile is not a stopgap, it is the control switched off.' That was written for the paneless branch; my remedy would have re-opened the same hole one branch over. NARROWED REMEDY: accept the claim only when the claimed pid is a live DESCENDANT OF THE PANE ROOT. `harness_process` already builds the full ps snapshot and walks that subtree, so the membership test is information it has computed and currently discards — returning it costs one value and no extra ps call. That preserves a self-registering omp/pi seat (its own pid is in the pane subtree by construction), refuses an unrelated live process, and keeps the evidence daemon-derived: the daemon still decides which processes exist and where they sit, and the claim only SELECTS among processes the daemon observed. Weaker but still strictly better than today, if the subtree is not threaded through: on `ProcSource::Pane`, REFUSE the registration rather than silently binding the seat to the pane shell — the refusal shape already exists at mod.rs:470-475. A refusal is loud and recoverable; a shell binding is silent and produces the announce bug. PLACEMENT HAZARD, separate and easy to miss: `pane_harness_identity` is SHARED by `register` and `adopt`, and it is the natural home for this fix because it is where ProcSource::Pane is decided — and it is the wrong home. Adopt's only claim is `CallerContext.pid`, marked at identity.rs:119-122 'DIAGNOSTIC ONLY. Never admissible as bind evidence.' If the preference is made uniform inside the shared helper, adopt inherits it and AC7's anti-impersonation control is gone with every gate still green. The preference must live in the `register` handler, or the helper must take the claim as a parameter with adopt passing None. CORRECTION TO MY REMEDY (c), derived from a live sweep rather than from the diff — and it REVERSES the axis I first named. I ported harness_command faithfully and evaluated it against all 1743 live processes on this machine: 106 plausible harness candidates, 87 accepted, 19 rejected, and the 19 point in opposite directions. CLASS A, 17 `bun.exe` rejects: correctly rejected. Every one is an omp INTERNAL worker (`__omp_worker_*`) parented to a real `bun …/bin/omp`, never a pane's top-level harness. So the package-path branch being unable to fire against `bun.exe` is, on this machine, HARMLESS — and widening the interpreter list to admit it would make 17 worker processes eligible as a pane's harness, which is a worse failure than the fallback because the wrong answer is live and plausible. CLASS B, 2 `node` rejects: a real missed top-level harness, and it is pij's own — `node …/@github/copilot/npm-loader.js … --allow-tool=pij_send`, parented to a tmux server pij created (`-S …/pij-copilot-native-79VliT/tmux.sock`). It is rejected because `file_stem` is `npm-loader`, which is not in `{cli, index}`, even though the package path matches. So the constraint that rejects a real pij-launched entrypoint is the STEM WHITELIST, not the interpreter list. Honest limitation, which lowers the severity: this does not currently cause a fallback, because the loader's child is `…/copilot-darwin-arm64/copilot`, whose basename matches on the first branch, so BFS finds it one level deeper. The value of the observation is that the `{cli,index}` whitelist is demonstrably WRONG on a real string rather than merely untested with one, and that only a natively-named child rescues it — a loader without one, which is the omp/pi-by-package-path shape, would not be rescued. COUNTERFACTUAL, run over the same live data: main (node|bun, stem in {cli,index}) accepts 87, admits 0 workers, misses the copilot loader; +bun.exe accepts 104 and admits 17 workers; any-interpreter with the stem kept accepts 104 and admits 17 workers; node|bun with the STEM CONSTRAINT DROPPED accepts 89, admits 0 workers, and matches the copilot loader; any-interpreter with the stem dropped accepts 106 and admits 17 workers. Remedy (c) is therefore REPLACED: keep the interpreter allowlist at node|bun and drop the `{cli,index}` stem constraint, requiring only the package path — `script.contains(package)`. Every variant that touches the interpreter list admits all 17 workers. The axis I originally told the PM to widen is the one that must not be; the constraint I never questioned is the one that is wrong.
value.receipt: grep for `proc_source|procSource` across all .rs/.ts excluding node_modules → only crates/daemon/src/http/{mod.rs:442,452,466,507, identity.rs:395,559} and identity_tests.rs:{262,314,376}; no TS occurrence. `harness_command` interpreter test is `executable != "node" && executable != "bun" → false` (crates/tmux/src/lib.rs). Live: `ps -Awwo pid=,ppid=,command= | grep -F "@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent"` → 8 rows whose argv[0] basename is `bun.exe`. `file ~/.npm-global/bin/omp` → `a /usr/bin/env bun script text executable`, which is why the shim path matches today. My own seat: `pij-rs state pij-wild-xoxarle` → pid 92715, and `ps` shows 92715 = `bun /Users/jordanknight/.npm-global/bin/omp …` with pane root 92699 = `pij-rs __spawn-child` — so the harness-child branch does work for the current launcher, which is exactly why the fallback is easy to miss. Adopt cannot reach the rule at all: with a pane it derives its own identity, and the paneless branch is refused outright (identity.rs:428-465), so the PM's 'adopt carries no claim' holds — for a stronger reason than stated. Claim liveness guard read at crates/daemon/src/registration.rs:67-87 (observes proc_start for the claimed pid; no pane relationship tested). CLI doctrine at crates/cli/src/main.rs:901-904: pid/proc_start 'deliberately NOT filled from this process'. Live sweep at main c46e2495: `ps -Awwo pid=,ppid=,command=` → 1743 processes; faithful port of harness_command over 106 candidates → 87 accept / 19 reject; rejected argv[0] basenames are bun.exe ×17 (all `__omp_worker_*`, all parented to `bun …/bin/omp`) and node ×2 (both `…/@github/copilot/npm-loader.js … --allow-tool=pij_send`, ppid 33336 = `tmux -S …/pij-copilot-native-79VliT/`). Five-variant counterfactual table computed over the same snapshot. INSTRUMENT SELF-CHECK, because the counterfactual table is now driving a code change and the table is only as good as my port of the predicate: I ran all 11 cases pinned by the Rust unit test `harness_commands_match_entrypoints_not_prompt_arguments` through the Python port — 0 disagreements — and re-confirmed the six load-bearing verdicts individually (main rejects the copilot npm-loader and accepts my own `bun …/bin/omp`; variant C accepts the loader and still rejects an `__omp_worker_*`; variant A with bun.exe accepts that worker). A reversal argued from an unverified instrument is just a different guess.

value.finding: A one-token regression turned 'skip a bad directory entry' into 'abandon discovery'. The pre-fix scan was `fs::read_dir(...).ok()?.filter_map(std::result::Result::ok).map(|e| e.path())` — an errored DirEntry was SKIPPED and the scan continued. The new loop opens with `let path = entry.ok()?.path();`, and that `?` is inside `discover`, which returns `Option<Endpoint>` — so a single errored DirEntry now returns None from the WHOLE function, discarding every candidate that had not yet been examined, including ones already known to be live. The consequence is the failure mode this plan is trying to eliminate: discovery reports 'no endpoint', delivery falls back to pointer-drain, and nothing says why. This is a genuinely rare input (readdir on a directory whose entries are churning), but the cost of the correct form is one line and the current form is strictly worse than what it replaced. SMALLEST FIX: `let Ok(entry) = entry else { continue; };`. Worth stating that everything ELSE about this function's rewrite is an improvement, and I checked the parts I expected to break: the local-vs-UTC timebase split is correct and deliberate (descriptor `proc_start` is LOCAL because `ProcLiveness` runs `ps` without TZ; Claude's recorded `procStart` is UTC; the code observes each in its own timebase and `parse_process_start` explicitly refuses to convert), and the ambiguity rule — two live records matching one pane returns None rather than picking one — is the right call and is tested three ways.
value.receipt: git diff 4b000ffb^1 4b000ffb -- crates/transport/src/uds.rs: removed line `.filter_map(std::result::Result::ok)`, added `let path = entry.ok()?.path();`. `cargo test -p pij-store --test store_registry` and the daemon suite exercise no readdir-error path; there is no witness for this branch.

value.finding: AC7's promise is TRUE and the reported problem is STILL LIVE — because the fix is not retroactive and nothing sweeps. The plan says so explicitly ('Existing rows are not rewritten — a re-adopt fixes a seat'), so this is not a broken promise; it is the gap between 'the unit is done' and 'the incident is closed', and it is worth a row because the live-proof reads as if the fleet were remediated ('18 of 19 live Claude seats bound to their pane's shell … fixed and measured end to end' — what was measured was one NEW adopt). I audited the actual fleet on this machine at main tip: of 52 registered Claude seats, 31 have a dead pid, 3 are bound to a real `claude` process, and 18 ARE STILL BOUND TO A SHELL. All 18 have a live `claude` descendant under the recorded pid right now, so all 18 would bind correctly on a re-adopt — and nothing performs one. Compounding it, and this is the same root as f2: there is no way for an operator to ASK which seats are shell-bound, because `proc_source` has no consumer and the descriptor exposes only a pid. The observable today is indirect (a delivery that lands via pointer-drain instead of claude-uds). Naming this for prime rather than expanding the review: the missing piece is a re-adopt sweep, or a liveness/adopt path that notices the recorded pid is not the harness process and rebinds.
value.receipt: Computed by me from `pij-rs list --json` joined against `ps -Awwo pid=,ppid=,command=` at main 5b40ed76: 52 claude seats; pid runs claude = 3; pid is a shell = 18; pid dead = 31. Descendant walk over the same ps snapshot: 18 of 18 shell-bound seats have a live `claude` descendant (e.g. pij-anxious-toucan pid 92181 `-zsh` → child 97554 `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`; pij-capitalist-boa 86295 → 90167; pij-equal-sparrow 73088 → 93161).

value.finding: AC8's second half is a property of code nothing calls. The claim is that omp/pi seats 'render the rs frame AND still PARSE the legacy `[pij from <id>] …` head'. The rendering half is true and load-bearing — `frame()` has two production callers (core/session.ts:593 on inbound inject, core/daemon/router.ts:41 in injectionText). The parsing half is not: `parseFrame` has ZERO production callers anywhere in the repository. Its only non-definition occurrences are in core/message.test.ts. That is structurally unsurprising — the extension receives peer messages as `message.pushed` daemon events carrying `from` and `body` as separate fields, and frames on INJECT, so it never has a framed string to parse — but it means the legacy-parse compatibility AC8 promises is unreachable at runtime and its regression surface is a test asserting against an unused function. Not false, but its operational value is nil, and it will rot. Either wire it to a real inbound path or say plainly in the plan that it is a library affordance retained for the migration reader, so a later reader does not infer that live legacy frames are being handled.
value.receipt: grep -rn 'parseFrame' over all .ts/.js excluding node_modules and *.test.ts → exactly one hit: `.pi/extensions/pij/core/message.ts:17` (the definition). grep for `frame(` → production callers core/session.ts:593, core/daemon/router.ts:41.

value.finding: Two halves of this plan disagree about what to do with ambiguity, and the inconsistency is worth naming even though the reachable risk is small. In crates/transport/src/uds.rs the authors wrote the rule down explicitly — 'Multiple live owners are ambiguous, never decided by directory or lexical order' — and made two live candidates return None, with three tests pinning it including one that renames a file to prove sort order cannot resolve it. In crates/tmux/src/lib.rs the same class of ambiguity IS resolved by enumeration order: two harness descendants at the SAME breadth-first depth are decided by whichever `ps -A` printed first, silently. Breadth-first ordering does most of the work (a nested harness is deeper, so the direct child wins, and that IS tested), so I could not construct a realistic same-depth case for the harnesses in play — which is why this is a NIT and not a defect. But if the uds rule is doctrine, the tmux walk should either refuse a same-depth tie or state in a comment why order is acceptable here.
value.receipt: uds.rs comment + `if candidate.is_some() { return None; }` and test `two_live_pane_records_require_exact_identity_not_sort_order`; tmux/lib.rs `for (proc, ppid, command) in processes { … return Some(*proc) }` with no tie check, test `descendant_walk_is_breadth_first_and_falls_back_only_to_the_pane` covering depth but not a same-depth tie.

value.finding: `PutBinding.previous_proc: None` carries two different facts and the handler collapses them. ports.rs documents the overload honestly ('`None` can also mean an unbound row'), and `inserted` disambiguates the created case. What is left undisambiguated: a row that EXISTED with no process identity, re-registered by a claim that also carries no process identity, yields `previous_proc (None) == descriptor.proc (None)` → `binding: same` → announce suppressed for what may well be a new process. Unreachable through the extension, which always sends pid and proc_start, and unreachable through the pane path, which now always resolves an identity or refuses; reachable in principle through a paneless `pij register` with no pid. Recorded rather than raised because the correct behaviour is arguable — a registration that declines to identify its process has arguably forfeited the right to be called fresh — but the code should say which reading it intends.
value.receipt: crates/store/src/registry.rs put_reporting builds `PutBinding { inserted: previous.is_none(), previous_proc: … }`; crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs derives `if report.inserted { Created } else if report.previous_proc != descriptor.proc { Rebound } else { Same }`. Store test `put_reporting_distinguishes_created_placeholder_rebound_and_same` covers unbound→bound (rebound) but not unbound→unbound.

value.finding: LEAST-CONFIDENT AREA (a) — uds discovery. VERDICT: one MINOR defect (f3), otherwise sound, and the part the authors were most worried about is the part they got right. The question was whether the live-record preference can now pick NOTHING although a usable record exists, or still pick a stale one. Stale: no — both paths gate on `live_endpoint`, which re-observes the process and refuses on mismatch, and the exact-identity path additionally requires `record.pid == proc.pid` and a LOCAL-timebase match against the descriptor. Nothing: yes, in exactly one input class, and that is f3 (an errored DirEntry aborts the scan). Everything else I probed came back clean. Specifically the timebase split, which is the subtlest thing in this diff and is CORRECT: the descriptor's `proc_start` is local wall time because `ProcLiveness` runs `ps -o lstart=` without TZ, while Claude's recorded `procStart` is UTC; the code observes each in its own timebase (`observe_start(pid, false)` vs `observe_start(record.pid, true)` with `TZ=UTC`), and `parse_process_start` is documented and tested to encode the supplied fields WITHOUT conversion. On a UTC-offset machine like this one a naive single-timebase comparison would have failed silently, and there is a dedicated test (`supplied_wall_time_is_encoded_without_timezone_conversion`) pinning the non-conversion. Also checked and clean: exact-identity failure falls through to the pane scan rather than terminating; the ambiguity rule returns None rather than guessing.
value.receipt: Read of uds.rs at 4b000ffb plus crates/core/src/model.rs parse_process_start and crates/harnesses/src/proc.rs (which now re-exports it). Tests `discovery_prefers_live_identity_over_first_dead_pane_record`, `recycled_records_and_stale_exact_bindings_are_rejected`, `two_live_pane_records_require_exact_identity_not_sort_order`.

value.finding: LEAST-CONFIDENT AREA (b) — the harness tree walk. VERDICT: the three sub-questions asked all answer well; the defect is elsewhere in the same function and is f2. Two candidate descendants: breadth-first, so the direct child beats a nested one, and that is tested — a same-DEPTH tie falls to enumeration order, which is n1. A re-parented child: the walk is by ppid over a single snapshot with a `parents.contains` guard, so a cycle cannot hang it and a child re-parented to init simply is not found (fallback). A harness that died between registration and the walk: handled explicitly and well — `harness_process` re-observes the SELECTED pid with a second `ps` and returns None unless the start time still matches, which closes the TOCTOU that would otherwise let a recycled pid through. And the question I was asked to check specifically — is `proc_start` captured from the child or accidentally from the shell — is captured from the CHILD: `selected` is the child's own `ProcIdentity`, parsed from the child's own `ps` row by `process_row`, and re-verified against the child's pid. I verified that live on myself: my seat's registered identity is pid 92715 / 20260905112934, which is `bun …/bin/omp`, not the pane root 92699 (`pij-rs __spawn-child`). The residual risk is not in the walk but in the RECOGNISER and in what happens when it fails silently — f2.

value.finding: LEAST-CONFIDENT AREA (c) — the `same` derivation. VERDICT: checked, no defect found, and the specific sub-question has a defensible answer. `fresh = input.fresh ?? (liveDescriptor === null || wasDissolved)` means a PRESENT binding fully overrides the local inference, including when the local registry row is MISSING. Suppressing the announce in that case is correct, and for a sharper reason than 'the daemon is authoritative': `same` means the daemon's stored row already carries THIS EXACT pid AND proc_start, which can only be true if this same process incarnation already registered — i.e. a reload, whose announce has already fired. A missing local row in that situation means the extension's roster view is incomplete, not that the process is new. The ordering also holds: the roster is seeded from `seats` BEFORE `session.boot` and the accepted descriptor is seeded after, so `liveDescriptor` is a genuine pre-boot view and the override is not shadowing a value it just wrote. Is `same` ever wrong for a genuinely NEW process? Not through this derivation — a new process has a new (pid, proc_start) pair, so `previous_proc != descriptor.proc` and the answer is `rebound`. It can be wrong only if the identity WRITTEN is not the harness's, which is f2's failure mode, not this one's. `undefined` correctly preserves the old-daemon inference (risk r2) and is tested.

value.finding: LEAST-CONFIDENT AREA (d) — the cross-harness samePane guard. VERDICT: checked, no defect found; both halves of the question answer cleanly. Does harness equality use a value that is reliably present? Yes — `input.runtimeBin` is typed `"pi" | "omp"` and is NON-optional on `RustBootInput` (rust-runtime.ts:32), so it can never be undefined; and it is the SAME value the seat registers as its harness (`registrationFor` sets `harness: input.runtimeBin`, line 348). The comparison is therefore within one domain rather than across two vocabularies, which is the usual way this kind of guard rots. Can a legitimate same-harness reuse be refused? No — an omp seat's stored `harness` is always `"omp"` because the extension itself wrote it, and a `pij-rs spawn --harness omp` row is likewise `"omp"`; the predicate matches. The guard only excludes rows whose harness genuinely differs, which is the intent. One thing I checked and want on the record because it looks like a hole and is not: the `sameProcess` fallback immediately below has NO harness guard, but it keys on `(process.pid, procStart)` of the CURRENT process, which no other seat can hold, so it is not a second hijack path.

value.finding: LEAST-CONFIDENT AREA (e) — the frame parser. VERDICT: checked, no defect found, and I probed it by execution rather than by reading the regex. Body round-trip is CLEAN for every hostile class asked about and several more: a body containing a literal `[/pij]`, a body ENDING in `[/pij]`, a body that is nothing but `[/pij]`, embedded CRLF, trailing space, trailing newline, empty body, and a body that contains a complete forged frame. The greedy `([\s\S]*)` is what saves the embedded-tail cases — it binds to the LAST `\n[/pij]` before end-of-input, so the outer frame always wins and an inner forged head never captures `from`. The second half of the question — can a MALFORMED frame be parsed as a valid one — answers in the safe direction: mutating a complete frame (append `\n`, append a space, normalise to CRLF) yields NULL, not a misparse, because JavaScript's `$` without the `m` flag anchors strictly at end-of-input. So the failure mode is refusal, never silent corruption. Two observations that are not defects: `([^\]]+)` permits a newline inside the sender id, which is inherited from the legacy pattern and unreachable for real ids; and the Rust framer can emit a machine-qualified head (`[pij-rs from <id>@<machine>]`) that the TS framer never produces, an asymmetry that also predates this plan and that `parseFrame` handles by capturing the whole `id@machine` string (pinned by a test).

value.finding: LEAST-CONFIDENT AREA (f) — atomicity of the reported binding. VERDICT: checked, no defect found; this is the best-defended part of the diff. The pre-read (`SELECT pid, proc_start FROM seats WHERE id = ?1`) is issued INSIDE the transaction opened by `begin_write`, which is `pool.begin_with("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")` — so the write lock is held from before the read until commit, and no other writer can interleave between the observation and the write it describes. There is therefore no path where the reported binding and the committed row disagree: they are decided under one lock and committed together, and a rollback loses both. The half-identity guard was factored out into `row_proc` and reused rather than reimplemented, so the pre-read refuses a pid-without-proc_start row exactly as `row_to_descriptor` always did — a detail that matters, because a silently-`None` half identity would have read as 'unbound' and produced a wrong `rebound`. And the property is tested against a real SQLite file with two independent pools racing, asserting that the second writer observes the first writer's COMMITTED proc, not a pre-race snapshot.

value.finding: SEAM 2: the one seam that carries a real defect, and it is f2. The question asked was whether `put_reporting` still reports the TRUTH now that the recorded proc is the harness child rather than the pane shell. Mechanically, yes: the register handler mutates `request.claim` BEFORE `RegistrationService` builds the descriptor, and `put_reporting` compares the stored proc against that same descriptor, so both sides of the comparison live in one vocabulary and the report describes what was written. I also checked the MIGRATION direction, which nobody named: rows written before u3 hold PANE SHELL identities, so the first registration after the upgrade compares shell-against-harness-child and returns `rebound` — one extra announce per seat across the cutover. That is benign and arguably correct (it IS a new binding). The dangerous direction is the reverse — stored shell identity plus a walk that falls back to the shell again, yielding `same` for a new process — and that is f2. So: the report is truthful about what it wrote; the defect is in WHAT gets written when discovery fails, and in nothing observing that it failed.

value.finding: The timebase split is correctly implemented and its WITNESS loses all discriminating power on a UTC host. The design is right: `process_start(pid, utc)` runs `ps -o lstart=` with `TZ=UTC` only when comparing against Claude's UTC-recorded `procStart`, and without it when comparing against a descriptor's locally-observed `proc_start`. I verified `ps` genuinely honours TZ on this platform rather than assuming it — default `Sat Sep  5 11:29:34 2026`, `TZ=UTC` `Sat Sep  5 01:29:34 2026`, `TZ=Asia/Tokyo` `10:29:34` — so the two observations really are different numbers here (20260905112934 vs 20260905012934) and an implementation that swapped or dropped the flag would fail. The NIT: that is a property of THIS HOST, not of the test. The updated fixture writes `procStart` under `TZ=UTC` and the seat's `proc_start` from local `ProcLiveness`, so on a host where local == UTC the two values coincide and the witness cannot distinguish a correct implementation from one that ignores the split entirely. CI runners are conventionally UTC, which is precisely where this would go quietly green. Cheapest hardening is to make the discriminator explicit rather than ambient — assert in the test that the local and UTC observations DIFFER (skipping or xfailing when they do not), so a UTC host reports 'this property was not exercised here' instead of 'this property holds'. Recorded as a NIT because the implementation is correct and the test is not wrong; it is a witness whose strength depends on where it runs, which is the same class as a fixture whose answer depends on who wrote it.
value.receipt: Measured on this host (date +%z = +1000): `env LC_ALL=C ps -p <pid> -o lstart=` → 11:29:34; `env LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC …` → 01:29:34; `TZ=America/New_York` → Fri 21:29:34; `TZ=Asia/Tokyo` → 10:29:34. NOTE ON METHOD: my first attempt at this measurement used a different shell quoting form and reported local and UTC as IDENTICAL, which would have made `observe_start`'s utc flag look inert and Claude discovery look broken on every non-UTC host — a MAJOR finding. I re-measured with `env` before reporting anything, and the second measurement contradicted the first. The claim was never sent. Recorded because the near-miss is the point: a one-command measurement is an instrument too.

(from|watchdog)`, which accepts BOTH generations rather than swapping one for the other — the correct migration shape for a scanner that must read historical transcripts as well as current ones.
